IAS officer Sajjan Singh Yadav assumes charge as Chief Secretary of J&K
 He joins at a time when the Chief Secretary post acts as the main interface between the Lok Bhavan and the Chief Minister’s office in the Union Territory (UT)
 Published - November 18, 2026 11:37 pm IST - Srinagar 
 The Hindu Bureau READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Dr. Sajjan Singh Yadav pictured taking charge of the office. Photo: X/@diprjk
 Dr. Sajjan Singh Yadav, a senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of 1995 batch, on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) formally took charge as the Chief Secretary of J&K.
 Officials said senior administrative secretaries welcomed Mr. Yadav at the Civil Secretariat, Jammu. He made his first appearance at a police function held at the Sher-I-Kashmir Police Academy, Udhampur.
 On October 24, 2026, Mr. Yadav was assigned the job. He joins at a time when the Chief Secretary post acts as the main interface between the Lok Bhavan and the Chief Minister’s office in the Union Territory (UT). Picked from the Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territories (AGMUT) cadre, Mr. Yadav’s will have to handle the most sticky files, including the Cabinet-approved files on regularisation of daily wagers, rationalisation of reservation and finalisation of Transaction of Business Rules, which remains undecided even after two years of completion of the Omar Abdullah government on October 16.
 Mr. Yadav, a resident of Haryana, has a doctorate in Public Health from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and Master’s in Public Policy, University of Minnesota. He brings in multi-sectoral experience as he served as Mission Director, National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyan); Director, National Rural Health Mission; Commissioner of Food & Civil Supplies, Trade and Taxes, Excise in Delhi. This year, Mr. Yadav also served as Delhi Additional Chief Secretary and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Delhi Jal Board.
